body:
Feedback from Bart Preneel about approved KEX schemes:

> RSA is not a KEX but a public key encryption scheme.
> 
> What should be listed are KEMs as standardized a.o. by ISO: RSA-KEM

comments.body: I am wondering if the intent in mentioning "RSA" under key exchange mechanism was to include the "RSA transport" TLS key exchange (where some key material is sent to the remote peer by encrypting it using RSAES-PKCS1-v1_5). @danielcuthbert any idea?

This one is still relevant.

Currently we have this snippet:

> A security strength of 128 bits or above MUST be ensured for all Key Exchange schemes, and their implementation MUST follow the parameter choices in the next table:
> 
> | Scheme | Domain Parameters |
> |--|--|
> | <mark>RSA</mark> | k >= 3072 |
> | Diffie-Hellman (DH) | L >= 3072 & N >= 256 |
> | Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) | f >= 256-383 

I think, the intent here is to mention the usage of [RSA Key Exchange](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5246#appendix-F.1.1.2) as defined in TLS.

As implemented in TLS v1.2, this does not provide forward secrecy anyway so I am wondering if this should be approved anyway. Maybe it should be included as **allowed for legacy** (see #2573)?
I think it should be approved, you are right and there is the legacy option too. Can you add this into that PR?
